body.heading: Paint your pictures
paragraphs: Choose smooth, flat stones and wash and dry them first. Paint one simple picture on each stone — a sun, a boat, a cat, a key, a tree, a star.
Simple pictures are best. A story stone needs to whisper ideas, not shout a whole story by itself.

body.heading: Tell a stone story
paragraphs: Put your stones in a bag. Pull out three without looking and line them up. Now tell a story that travels through all three pictures.
If you pulled the cat, the boat, and the star, your story might sail a cat across the sea under the stars. Every pull makes a different tale.

body.heading: Grow the collection
paragraphs: Add new stones whenever you find a good one — a dragon, a door, a mountain. More stones mean more stories hiding in the bag.
Stories live in storytellers, not in stones. The stones just give your imagination a friendly push.

takeaway: Painted story stones turn three random pictures into a brand-new story every time.
materials: Paints or paint pens (an adult helps)
safetyNotes: Use big stones that are too large to be a choking hazard, and keep stones away from very young children. Wash hands after painting, and let an adult tidy the paints.
screenFreeExtension: Tell a whole story using only three stones, then swap one stone and tell how the story changes.
